summary.title: Linux Command Line Computing
summary.one_liner: A free online book that teaches Linux command line tools and shell scripting, focused on managing files and text processing, for beginner to intermediate users.
takeaways: The book targets beginner to intermediate users and assumes basic programming knowledge such as variables, loops and functions.
Its main focus is managing files and performing text processing with Linux command line tools and bash.
System administration and networking are explicitly excluded from the scope.
Examples are based on bash 5.0.17, and the book recommends reading manuals and searching online for help.
Example files and exercises are available in the cli-computing GitHub repo, and the book is licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
summary.summary: This is the preface of an online book, mdBook-built, by Sundeep Agarwal on Linux command line tools and shell scripting. It describes the target audience (beginner to intermediate), the prerequisites (basic computer use and programming basics), and the working environment (GNU bash on Linux, a VM, or WSL). It also covers conventions such as code snippets copied from bash 5.0.17, the companion GitHub repo with example files and exercises, and how to report errata. The page is mostly front matter, with the author bio, license and acknowledgements.
